cards.q: What is an LER and where does it sit in the MPLS domain?
cards.a: The LER (also called PE in VPN terms) sits at the edge of the MPLS domain. It does the IP-to-label transition, pushing a label on ingress and popping it on egress, and runs the full IP routing stack (IGP plus MP-BGP for VPNs).

cards.q: What are the LER's edge responsibilities by direction?
cards.a: On ingress it classifies then pushes a label; on egress it pops the label and delivers IP; the core side faces MPLS (the LSP) and the CE side faces the customer.

cards.q: What are the ingress LER steps for forwarding a packet?
cards.a: Receive IP from CE, do a CEF lookup to find the FEC, push the transport label (plus service label if VPN), then forward into the core. The push is decided by the FEC.

cards.q: What are the egress LER steps for delivering a packet?
cards.a: Receive the labeled packet from the core, pop the label (after PHP), route or deliver to the CE, with VRFs separating customers.

cards.q: Why does the egress LER often receive an explicit null with PHP?
cards.a: Because with PHP the label has already been popped, so the egress often receives an explicit null to keep the Exp (QoS) field.

cards.q: What roles combine to make an LER act as a PE in a VPN?
cards.a: The PE is an LER that also runs VRF (per-customer routing table), MP-BGP (exchange VPNv4 routes), LDP (core label), and CE-facing PE-CE routing.

cards.q: In an LER configuration, how are core-facing and CE-facing interfaces handled?
cards.a: Core-facing interfaces get 'mpls ip', while CE-facing interfaces go into a VRF using 'ip vrf forwarding' with an IP address.

cards.q: What commands verify VRF and label forwarding on an LER?
cards.a: show ip cef, show mpls forwarding-table, show ip vrf, show ip vrf detail, and show ip route vrf CUST1.

cards.q: What is the likely cause and check when there is no label push on a router?
cards.a: The cause is CEF or FEC missing, so check show ip cef.

cards.q: What is the likely cause and check when a CE is unreachable?
cards.a: The VRF may be missing or the interface not bound, so check show ip vrf.

cards.q: How does the LER position map to the quick review table?
cards.a: The LER is at the edge, pushes on ingress, pops on egress, acts as the PE in a VPN, uses a VRF on the CE side, applies 'mpls ip' on the core side, runs IGP plus MP-BGP for routing, and classifies packets into FECs.
